clue.text: Takes a hand when it comes to a fight

definitions.text: Takes a hand when it comes to a fight

parts.words: Takes a hand when it comes to a fight
parts.note: the item described is padded wear that holds a boxer's fist while sparring or in the ring

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's padded mitt literally takes in the hand whenever a bout begins.

clue.text: Should and could be tough

indicators.note: the letters of tough could be rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: Something you are obliged to do might turn out to be hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought and should both express obligation, as in 'you ought to go'.

clue.text: Raise one pound somehow for a citizen of a modern state

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some unstated new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Somebody gathers a quid for a national of a young country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges RAISE with I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel was founded in 1948, so its nationals belong to a modern state.

clue.text: Ploy that's some game with a little piece

indicators.note: only some of the word game is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A tactic involves playing a bit with a small piece on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' drops the final E of GAME. A gambit is also a chess opening that sacrifices a pawn, so 'piece' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move or stratagem meant to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Feed about one

definitions.meaning: at roughly one o'clock, midday mealtime

explanation.definitionFit: Luncheon is a formal midday meal, typically eaten around one o'clock.

clue.text: Cover a way of living around the East

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit around the next piece
a way of living means the word living arranged in another way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A lifestyle wraps itself about the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a way of' rearranges LIVING to VILING, and 'around' puts E inside it after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: Veiling is material used as a covering, such as fine net or gauze.

clue.text: Support an opinion with a wager

definitions.text: Support an opinion with a wager

parts.words: Support an opinion with a wager
parts.note: to place a bet on a personal hunch, putting money behind a favourite

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to bet on what you personally fancy, standing behind your own judgement.

clue.text: Succeeds in getting an open air living?

definitions.meaning: earns a living out of doors

explanation.definitionFit: Make out means manage, and read literally it is earning one's keep outside.

clue.text: It's folly so to speak

parts.note: foolish talk, and the verb meaning speak placed before talk that lacks sense

explanation.definitionFit: Utter nonsense is complete rubbish, and to utter is to speak.

clue.text: A sort of guru or seer

indicators.note: a 'sort of' guru is the word guru put into another order of letters

explanation.surface: A mystic teacher is compared to a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges GURU to UGUR, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman priest who foretold events, so a prophet or seer.

clue.text: Apparently he admits he's unable to improve, poor beggar

parts.note: to mend something is to repair or improve it
a man owning up that he cannot says 'I can't'

explanation.surface: A down-and-out confesses he cannot better himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' tells you the answer, read as a phrase, says 'mend? I can't'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone who lives by begging, often a friar of a begging order.

clue.text: Frolicsome as a young scratch player

definitions.meaning: like a young cat, an animal that scratches while it plays

explanation.definitionFit: Kittenish means playful, the way a young cat romps and claws at things.

clue.text: Girl encased in wrath

annotationWithheld.why: 'Girl encased in wrath (5)' as held: 'wrath' cannot hide or build IRENE (IRE plus NE has no source); the printed hiding phrase seems misread and no scan is held

clue.text: Cloth protection for sleepy little brethren

parts.note: a nap is a little sleep
kin are one's relatives, brothers and the like

explanation.surface: A blanket is laid over drowsy small siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: A napkin is a cloth laid on the lap to protect clothing while eating.

clue.text: No amateur at knotting ropes to whom Ariel was bound to be grateful

definitions.text: to whom Ariel was bound to be grateful

parts.note: a professional, a pro, is not an amateur

indicators.note: knotting tangles the word ropes into a new order

explanation.surface: An expert in rope knots receives thanks from a sprite bound to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knotting' rearranges ROPES to SPERO. In The Tempest, Prospero freed the spirit Ariel, who then served him.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's magician released Ariel from a cloven pine, earning the spirit's gratitude and service.

clue.text: How budding snooker players are raised in the nursery?

definitions.text: How budding snooker players are raised in the nursery?

parts.words: How budding snooker players are raised in the nursery?
parts.note: a garden nursery raises young plants in containers, and snooker players sink balls into the pockets they call pots

explanation.definitionFit: Pot-grown describes a plant raised in a container rather than in open ground.

clue.text: Make a mark as a man of letters in the first place

parts.note: taken as written
a scribe is a professional writer or copyist

explanation.surface: Becoming famous as a writer starts with signing one's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the first place' is an instruction: the word 'in' is set at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To inscribe is to write or engrave characters on a surface.

clue.text: Goes on one leg, saving money perhaps

definitions.meaning: a hosiery item that is pulled onto a single leg
laying up a hoard of cash, as in the old habit of keeping savings in a sock

explanation.definitionFit: A stocking is hosiery for a leg, and stocking up is building up a store.

clue.text: Doesn't miss the shows, just for show

definitions.meaning: keeps attending public performances, literally maintaining one's turns on stage
maintaining a front so outsiders see nothing amiss

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keeping up a pretence of normality, and read literally it is still turning up to perform.

clue.text: Unable to get on in old Kwangchow

parts.note: unable means one can't
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cannot make progress in a Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Kwangchow, now Guangzhou, is the Chinese port long known in the West by the older name.
explanation.definitionFit: Canton was the European name for the southern Chinese city of Guangzhou.

clue.text: Flapper on the plane in a role that's different

indicators.note: the letters of in a role are taken differently, into a new order

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper takes on a new role while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's different' rearranges IN A ROLE. 'Flapper' suggests a 1920s girl; it is a hinged flap on a wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged surface on an aircraft wing that controls roll.

clue.text: Sunshine worth 22p now" nowadays

annotationWithheld.why: 'Sunshine worth 22p now" nowadays (6)' as held: the OCR has garbled the second definition (a tanner was the old sixpence, 2½p), more than three letters off and no scan to confirm

clue.text: Concoction of Granny Smith and a Bronte

parts.note: a Granny Smith is a green variety of the fruit
Charlotte was the eldest of the Bronte sisters, author of Jane Eyre

explanation.surface: A recipe mixes an old woman named Smith with a Victorian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny Smith' looks like a person beside the novelist; it is the eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple charlotte is a baked dessert of fruit in a bread-lined mould, a concoction of the kitchen.

clue.text: See 23
What's yours in the old fashioned way

definitions.text: What's yours in the old fashioned way

parts.words: What's yours in the old fashioned way
parts.note: the archaic second-person possessive, as in the King James Bible

explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic form meaning belonging to you.

clue.text: Bunyan's progressive dream hero

parts.note: The Pilgrim's Progress is told as a dream, and its central pilgrim journeys onward to the Celestial City

explanation.definitionFit: Christian is the protagonist of John Bunyan's allegory, The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: Edges round a point in France

definitions.text: Edges round a point in France

indicators.note: the edges go round, enclosing what follows

parts.note: rims are edges
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Borders encircle a spot somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts E inside RIMS; the whole clue also points to the French cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Reims is a city in the Champagne region of north-east France.

clue.text: See 19
